metadata.title: The Last Rocket of Founding Day

setup.pitch: Founding Day is supposed to end with seven signal rockets fired from the old fort. Someone has rewired the launch racks, and the final rocket now points at the packed harbor instead of the sky.
setup.gmSummary: Brightwater's Founding Day commemorates the night seven warning rockets saved the town from a coastal raid. Modern celebrations reenact the signals with harmless festival fireworks launched from the old cliff fort. This year councilor Darric Vale ordered the signal sequence modernized into a synchronized harbor spectacle. Contractor Sera Flint quietly reused deteriorated military launch tubes to cut costs, while activist dockworker Bren Oss sabotaged one rack intending only to force cancellation and draw attention to unsafe working conditions. Their separate choices interact catastrophically: the seventh rocket's guidance cradle now points toward the harbor fuel barges, and several earlier rockets can ignite old powder stores beneath the fort. The party must uncover both failures, evacuate or secure the harbor, repair or redesign the launch sequence, and decide whether Founding Day ends with a safe traditional signal, a new public-safety demonstration, or the permanent retirement of the explosive ritual.
setup.background: Brightwater's original seven rockets were emergency signals: one for sighting, one for evacuation, one for militia muster, one for harbor chain, one for fire crews, one for shelter, and one for all-clear. The modern festival reduced them to spectacle. Dockworkers have repeatedly complained that the fort powder tunnels and launch racks are unsafe. Bren sabotaged one guidance brace to force an inspection, not realizing Sera had connected the final rack to a larger demonstration charge. Darric suppressed the latest engineering report because canceling the fireworks would embarrass the council.
setup.campaignFrame: Captain Brune Holt leads Hearthford's visiting watch detail at Brightwater's Founding Day and puts the party on the launch-yard danger when the seventh rack turns toward the harbor. The party returns to Hearthford with Brune's trust shaped by how they handled public safety and blame.

quest.objective: Discover why the Founding Day rockets are unsafe, prevent mass harm, and decide how Brightwater will finish or replace the seven-signal tradition.
quest.stakes: A packed harbor, fuel barges, old powder tunnels, and thousands of festivalgoers are at risk; mishandling the truth could also turn labor anger into a scapegoat hunt.
quest.deadline: SEVEN SIGNALS: show seven rocket marks. Fill one after the square, launch yard, dockworks, powder tunnel, and fort tower; the sixth and seventh become final-scene pressure. If the seventh fills unresolved, the automated ignition reaches the final rack.
successConditions: The harbor is secured or evacuated.
The true interaction between sabotage, unsafe equipment, and suppressed warnings is uncovered.
The final signal is resolved through Fire Safe, Public Rewrite, or Retire.
failureConditions: The party knowingly allows the automated seventh launch to fire into an unsecured harbor.
The town scapegoats one person while the structural hazard remains active.

facts.text: The original seven rockets were functional emergency signals, not entertainment.
Sera Flint reused deteriorated military launch tubes and connected the final rack to an oversized demonstration charge.
Bren Oss bent one guidance brace to force cancellation, but did not intend to aim a live rocket at the harbor.
Darric Vale suppressed an engineering report warning that the fort launch system and powder tunnels were unsafe.
The festival can end with a repaired safe signal sequence, a rewritten non-explosive public-safety demonstration, or permanent retirement of the rocket ritual.

secrets.text: Sera reused old military tubes because replacing them would have exceeded the council's fixed spectacle budget.
secrets.revealCondition: Read her invoice notes, inspect the tube serials, or confront her with the engineering report.

secrets.text: Bren sabotaged the brace to force inspection after three dockworkers were injured during setup.
secrets.revealCondition: Find his tool marks plus grievance letter, speak with injured workers, or confront him after the dockworks scene.

npcs.questFunction: Provides technical truth and a repair route without absolving unsafe cost-cutting.

locations.name: Brightwater Parade Square
locations.description: A crowded summer plaza of banners, marching bands, food carts, and a giant board showing the seven signal rockets scheduled for dusk.

locations.name: Old Fort Launch Yard
locations.description: Seven angled racks line the cliff wall beside fuse channels, water barrels, and a locked maintenance shed.

locations.name: Harbor Dockworks
locations.description: Fuel barges, fishing boats, worker cranes, and temporary festival seating pack the waterfront beneath the fort.

locations.name: Powder Tunnels
locations.description: Old military galleries beneath the fort hold sealed powder rooms, drainage channels, and one live ignition conduit feeding the modern display.

locations.name: Signal Tower
locations.description: The highest fort platform holds the master ignition wheel, signal lantern, and a panoramic view of harbor, racks, and evacuation routes.

clues.revelation: The seven rockets were originally emergency signals with specific public-safety meanings.
sources: A fort plaque lists SIGHTING / EVACUATE / MUSTER / CHAIN / FIRE / SHELTER / ALL-CLEAR.
The signal tower lantern has seven labeled shutter positions matching those actions.
Old parade programs show early festivals reenacting the response drills, not just fireworks.

clues.revelation: The launch system uses condemned military tubes and an oversized final charge.
sources: Tube serials match condemned numbers in the engineering report.
Sera's invoice notes REUSE EXISTING RACKS and DEMO CHARGE X2 beside the seventh rack.
A hairline split and heat scoring are visible on tube three.

clues.revelation: Bren bent one guidance brace to force cancellation but did not wire or enlarge the explosive charge.
sources: Tool marks match Bren's numbered dock wrench and are limited to the seventh guidance brace.
His grievance letter says STOP THE SHOW / FORCE INSPECTION and mentions no ignition work.
The fuse harness and charge connections show contractor work untouched by Bren's wrench.

clues.revelation: Darric suppressed a formal warning about both the launch racks and powder tunnels.
sources: A sealed engineering report bears RECEIVED on the council copy but no public action stamp.
The archive receipt shows Darric checked out the report before the festival vote.
The engineer's chalk marks in the tunnels match hazards named in the report.

clues.revelation: Founding Day can end with a repaired safe signal sequence, a rewritten non-explosive emergency demonstration, or retirement of the explosive ritual.
sources: The Signal Keeper states 'Fire safe. Rewrite. Retire.' after one original signal is restored.
The tower master board has ROCKET / LANTERN-BELL / SHUTDOWN positions for each signal.
A prior festival log records a storm year completed entirely with lantern shutters and bells.

scenes.title: Signal Seven Turns
scenes.purpose: Launch the public danger, establish the signal clock, and reveal that the problem is mechanical before blame settles on one suspect.
scenes.readAloud: The marching band hits its final note as a practice motor turns the seventh rocket rack on the cliff. It should point seaward and high. Instead the rack groans downward until its empty guide tube aims straight at the crowded harbor. Seven painted rocket icons light on the festival board. The first begins blinking.
gmNotes: Show SEVEN SIGNALS. Fill signal 1 when this scene ends.
No rocket fires yet; this is the visible warning before automatic ignition progresses.
DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) from the square or tower spyglass spots that only rack seven's angle is wrong. Failure changes nothing; Sera says it immediately at the launch yard.
Darric publicly blames sabotage before evidence is gathered. Do not let that become established truth.
Move the party to the launch yard with authority to inspect and pause crowd access.

scenes.title: Old Tubes, New Show
scenes.purpose: Expose unsafe equipment and distinguish sabotage from contractor/council failures.
scenes.readAloud: Seven launch racks stand along the cliff. Rack seven's guidance brace is visibly bent. Rack three is worse in a quieter way: a black hairline crack runs along its old military tube. Sera Flint kneels beside the fuse board, swearing under her breath as the second signal light begins to blink.
gmNotes: Fill signal 2 when this scene ends.

DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) or relevant tool proficiency identifies three separate issues: bent brace, condemned tube, oversized final charge. Failure still reveals the brace and crack; Sera's diagram exposes the charge.
The sabotage tool marks affect angle only. Fuse and charge work use different tools and predate the brace damage.
An engineering report number is stamped on the condemned tube, pointing to the council archive copy and tunnel markings.
Sera sends the party to the docks because the harbor must be secured regardless of who caused what.

scenes.title: The Harbor Under the Rack
scenes.purpose: Protect civilians, establish Bren's motive, and keep labor grievances separate from the explosive-system failures.
scenes.readAloud: The harbor is packed shoulder-to-shoulder beneath the fort. Fuel carts sit beside food stalls. Two barges fly festival flags. Dockworkers are already hauling hoses into position while one man shouts that the fireworks should have been canceled days ago. Above everyone, rack seven points down like a finger.
gmNotes: Fill signal 3 when harbor evacuation begins and signal 4 when fuel sources are secured or moved.

Run a three-job safety challenge: clear spectators, move fuel carts, open water lines. Each job can be solved by roleplay, spells, or DC 13 Athletics/Investigation/Persuasion as appropriate. Failure adds one HARBOR PRESSURE mark but the job remains retryable or solvable another way.
Bren's grievance letter and three injured workers establish motive for forcing cancellation.
DC 13 Insight on Bren: success shows guilt about the brace but genuine surprise about the oversized charge. Failure gives no false conclusion; tool evidence later proves scope.
A marked hatch under the ramp leads into the powder tunnels.

runSteps.title: Run three safety jobs
runSteps.text: The scene matters even if the mystery were solved already.

runSteps.title: Hear the labor grievance
runSteps.text: Unsafe setup hurt people before the sabotage.

runSteps.title: Open the tunnel route
runSteps.text: The next layer is suppressed structural risk.

scenes.title: The Report Was Right
scenes.purpose: Prove council suppression, remove secondary explosion risk, and provide a noncombat route to the finale.
scenes.readAloud: The old tunnel walls are striped with fresh engineer's chalk: CRACKED VENT. WET POWDER. DO NOT RUN LIVE IGNITION. Someone has run a bright new festival conduit straight through the warnings. Far ahead, a relay box ticks once each time another signal icon lights above.
gmNotes: Fill signal 5 when the live conduit is isolated or safely rerouted.

DC 14 Dexterity with thieves' tools or Intelligence (Arcana/Investigation) safely isolates the conduit. Failure causes a flash burn for 2d6 fire damage but also trips the relay open, preventing tunnel ignition.
The engineer markings match the suppressed report language exactly.
A sealed report copy in the maintenance box bears Darric's received stamp.
The Signal Keeper appears once the conduit is safe and demonstrates that lantern/bell signals can replace rockets.

runSteps.title: Match report to wall
runSteps.text: Suppression becomes physical fact.

runSteps.title: Cut secondary risk
runSteps.text: Failure hurts but still prevents catastrophic tunnel ignition.

runSteps.title: Reveal alternate signal system
runSteps.text: Lantern/bell rewrite is proven before the finale.

exitChoices.label: Climb to the Signal Tower

scenes.title: Signal Seven
scenes.purpose: Resolve the holiday through safe repair, public rewrite, or retirement while the automated launch clock advances.
scenes.readAloud: Wind snaps the Founding Day flags at the top of the fort. Below, the harbor is half-cleared and lit by emergency lanterns. The master board shows five signals complete. Six begins to blink. Rack seven still points toward the water. Beside the ignition wheel, a translucent watch officer raises a shuttered lantern. “Signal seven,” it says. “All-clear. Harbor not clear.”
gmNotes: Start with signals 5/7 complete. At initiative count 20, advance one signal unless a character uses an Action at the master board to pause one cycle with DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation/Arcana) or Dexterity with tinker's tools. On failure the signal advances normally.

FIRE SAFE: complete three repair jobs—straighten rack seven, remove/replace tube three, reduce final charge. Each Action uses DC 14 appropriate Athletics/Investigation/tool check. Prepared help from Sera/Bren can make one chosen job automatic. When all three are done, the original seven-signal sequence can fire safely at reduced charge.

REWRITE: complete three public-safety stations—lantern signal pattern, bell response, harbor drill. Each Action uses DC 14 History/Investigation/Persuasion or a concrete coordinated action. Three completed stations allow Founding Day to finish without explosives.

RETIRE: cut the master ignition wheel and ceremonial powder feed. Core Mechanism AC 15, 24 HP after one deliberate shutdown action; destroying it permanently ends the rocket tradition but leaves lantern/bell emergency signals intact.

If signal 7 would fire while unresolved, anyone at the master wheel gets one final reaction: DC 15 Dexterity with tools or Strength (Athletics) to jam the wheel. Success prevents launch and deals 2d6 lightning/fire from the mechanism; failure launches the rocket, but if harbor safety jobs were completed it hits empty water/fuel-free pier instead of causing mass casualties.
Directly destroying the master mechanism counts as Retire.

runSteps.text: All three are legal from the start.

scenes.title: Resolution: Seven Safe Signals
scenes.purpose: Reward repairing the system while restoring the original public-safety meaning.
scenes.readAloud: Seven rockets rise one at a time—smaller, higher, and farther from the harbor than the crowd expected. After each burst, a bell and lantern answer from below. When the seventh fades, the Signal Keeper salutes and disappears into the fort wall.
gmNotes: Award 220 gp total and four Brightwater Favor tokens.
Future rocket displays require engineering signoff and emergency-response rehearsal.
Bren faces consequences for sabotage, but the council report suppression and contractor shortcuts are publicly recorded too.

runSteps.title: Restore function
runSteps.text: Each signal is tied back to a safety action.

runSteps.title: Record reward
runSteps.text: Award 220 gp and Favor tokens.

scenes.title: Resolution: The Harbor Answers
scenes.purpose: Reward replacing explosive spectacle with a participatory safety ritual.
scenes.readAloud: No rocket launches. Instead seven lantern patterns sweep from the fort while bells answer from the harbor, the fire house, the shelter hall, and the bridge. For the final all-clear, the whole waterfront answers with hand lamps at once.
gmNotes: Award 240 gp total and the Harbor Signal token, granting advantage on one future Brightwater check involving coordination, evacuation, or public safety.
Founding Day becomes an annual emergency drill wrapped in celebration.
Sera may continue designing safe non-explosive effects.

runSteps.title: Make the rewrite participatory
runSteps.text: The town answers every signal.

runSteps.title: Record reward
runSteps.text: Award 240 gp and Harbor Signal token.

scenes.advanceWhen: The new signal protocol and rewards are recorded.

scenes.title: Resolution: No More Powder Above the Harbor
scenes.purpose: Respect permanent retirement while retaining emergency preparedness.
scenes.readAloud: The master wheel breaks with a shower of harmless brass teeth. Below, nobody cheers at first. Then the harbor bells ring the old seven meanings in sequence, and dockworkers answer with lanterns. The celebration continues without a single rocket.
gmNotes: Award 220 gp total.
The fort's explosive festival system is permanently retired.
Lantern and bell emergency signals remain active and become the legal civic standard.

runSteps.title: Keep the safety system
runSteps.text: Retiring fireworks does not erase the original emergency protocol.

runSteps.title: Record reward
runSteps.text: Award 220 gp.

scenes.advanceWhen: The new non-explosive standard and rewards are recorded.

encounters.name: Harbor Panic
encounters.summary: Crowds, fuel carts, and dock crews must be moved while the signal clock advances.
encounters.resolution: Complete evacuation, fuel, and water-line jobs through roleplay, checks, or magic.
encounters.talkOut: This is not a creature encounter; coordinated instructions and visible authority are the primary solution.
encounters.bypass: No safe bypass. The party can delegate jobs to Darric/Bren crews, but each delegated job still consumes time or resources.
encounters.objective: Reduce consequences if the final launch cannot be stopped.

encounters.name: Powder Tunnel Sparks
encounters.summary: Ignition leakage animates small fire motes around old powder rooms.
encounters.resolution: Isolate the conduit, smother the motes, or pass once the relay is tripped.
encounters.bypass: Trip the relay open; the motes fade when the conduit loses power.

encounters.name: Signal Seven Mechanism
encounters.summary: The automated launch sequence advances while the party repairs, rewrites, or destroys the festival system.
encounters.resolution: Complete Fire Safe, complete Rewrite, or destroy/disable the master mechanism.
encounters.talkOut: The Signal Keeper supports safe procedural changes but cannot stop the machine alone.
encounters.bypass: Fire Safe and Rewrite are complete noncombat routes.
encounters.objective: Finish Founding Day without turning civic tradition into mass-casualty spectacle.

puzzles.prompt: Match seven old fort symbols to their emergency meanings using plaque, lantern shutters, and parade records.
puzzles.solution: Sighting / Evacuate / Muster / Harbor Chain / Fire Crews / Shelter / All-Clear.
puzzles.bypass: DC 14 History or Investigation reconstructs the sequence immediately.
puzzles.failForward: The tower shutter labels give the meanings after one wrong match.

traps.trigger: Cut or reroute the powder-tunnel ignition conduit without isolating the relay.
traps.effect: DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 fire damage.
traps.failForward: The relay trips open either way, preventing tunnel ignition.

policies: No single culprit explains the crisis; sabotage, unsafe equipment, and suppressed warnings remain independently provable.
Harbor safety work changes final consequences even if the mechanical repair fails.
Failure costs time, injuries, or property risk but never removes every finale route.

routes.trigger: Darric is unavailable or refuses cooperation.
routes.response: The received report, archive receipt, and engineer markings prove suppression without him.
stateChanges: Evacuation can be directed through dock captains.

routes.response: Serial numbers, invoice notes, cracks, and setup diagrams establish unsafe reused equipment.
stateChanges: Fire Safe is harder but still possible.

routes.trigger: Bren flees or refuses to talk.
routes.response: Crew-numbered wrench marks, grievance letter, and limited brace damage prove scope and intent.

routes.trigger: The party skips harbor safety and enters tunnels directly.
routes.response: The finale remains solvable, but HARBOR PRESSURE begins at 2 and a failed seventh launch can damage property/fuel even if mass casualties are avoided.

routes.trigger: The party reaches the tower without understanding all routes.
routes.response: The master board shows ROCKET / LANTERN-BELL / SHUTDOWN positions and the Signal Keeper names Fire Safe, Rewrite, Retire.

pathPressure.principle: Prepared investigation and harbor work reduce final danger and automate repairs, while rushed play preserves all endings at higher risk.
prepared: Sera can make one Fire Safe repair automatic.
Bren can make straightening rack seven automatic.
Completed harbor safety jobs reduce consequences of an accidental seventh launch.
Tunnel work proves Rewrite is operational before the finale.
rushed: Skipping tunnels leaves secondary ignition active until someone spends a finale action to cut it.
Entering without technical evidence makes Fire Safe checks all mandatory.

cutOrder: If 25+ minutes behind, combine rack audit and report-number discovery in one launch-yard beat.
If 15+ minutes behind at docks, let competent NPC crews automatically complete one of the three safety jobs.
Never cut the multi-cause truth, harbor consequences, or three finale routes.
optionalOrder: Extra parade interactions before the first signal.
Detailed history of each original military rocket after meanings are clear.

endings.name: Seven Safe Signals
endings.result: The rocket tradition survives under engineering oversight and restored emergency meanings.

endings.name: No More Powder Above the Harbor

endings.result: Fireworks retire while lantern/bell emergency signaling remains the civic standard.

encounters.objective: Resolve Founding Day through Fire Safe, Rewrite, or Retire before the seventh launch.
encounters.start: Five signal marks are lit and the automated master wheel continues advancing.
encounters.bypass: Fire Safe and Rewrite are complete noncombat routes.

creatures.name: Master Launch Mechanism
creatures.trait: Shutdown Core: after one deliberate Retire action, AC 15, 24 HP; destroying it ends automated launch and permanently retires the rocket system.
creatures.tactics: Advance signal clock, arc at creatures manipulating controls, and lock repaired racks unless actions are coordinated.

encounters.end: Fire Safe completes, Rewrite completes, or the master mechanism is destroyed.

hazards.trigger: Work the live conduit before isolating relay power.
hazards.failForward: The relay trips open either way, preventing tunnel ignition.

hazards.trigger: Initiative count 20 while the system remains unresolved.
hazards.failure: Advance one signal mark unless a character successfully pauses the master board.
hazards.success: A successful pause check buys one cycle.
hazards.failForward: Harbor preparation changes consequences even if the seventh signal is reached.

rewards.reward: 220 gp total and four Brightwater Favor tokens.
240 gp total and the Harbor Signal token.

rewards.when: The rocket system is permanently disabled.
rewards.reward: 220 gp total; lantern/bell emergency signaling remains.

flowContract.principle: One summer civic-safety mystery: inspect the launch failure, protect the harbor, prove multiple causes, control the tunnels, then branch only at the final signal.

continuity.relationshipEffect: Update Captain Brune Holt's Hearthford relationship state based on how the party handled this night.
continuity.standaloneRule: The adventure still runs standalone; the Hearthford frame supplies continuity but is never required to solve the plot.
